require "rails_helper"

describe Relationable::RelatedListComponent do
  let(:proposal) { create(:proposal) }
  let(:user_proposal) { create(:proposal, title: "I am user related") }
  let(:machine_proposal) { create(:proposal, title: "I am machine related") }
  let(:component) { Relationable::RelatedListComponent.new(proposal) }

  before do
    Setting["feature.machine_learning"] = true
    Setting["machine_learning.related_content"] = true

    create(:related_content, parent_relationable: proposal, child_relationable: user_proposal)
    create(:related_content, parent_relationable: proposal,
                             child_relationable: machine_proposal,
                             machine_learning: true)
  end

  it "displays machine learning and user content when machine learning is enabled" do
    render_inline component

    expect(page).to have_css "li", count: 2
    expect(page).to have_content "I am machine related"
    expect(page).to have_content "I am user related"
  end

  it "displays user related content when machine learning is disabled" do
    Setting["feature.machine_learning"] = false

    expect(page).to have_css "li", count: 1
    expect(page).to have_content "I am user related"
    expect(page).not_to have_content "I am machine related"
  end

  it "displays user related content when machine learning related content is disabled" do
    Setting["machine_learning.related_content"] = false

    render_inline component

    expect(page).to have_css "li", count: 1
    expect(page).to have_content "I am user related"
    expect(page).not_to have_content "I am machine related"
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe ActsAsTaggableOn do
  describe "Tagging" do
    describe "when tagging debates or proposals" do
      let(:proposal) { create(:proposal) }
      let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

      it "increases and decreases the tag's custom counters" do
        tag = Tag.create!(name: "foo")

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        proposal.tag_list.add("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        debate.tag_list.add("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        proposal.tag_list.remove("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        debate.tag_list.remove("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "Tag" do
    describe "public_for_api scope" do
      it "returns tags whose kind is NULL and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: nil)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "returns tags whose kind is 'category' and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, :category)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "blocks other kinds of tags" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: "foo")
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "blocks tags that don't have at least one tagged element" do
        create(:tag)

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "only permits tags on proposals or debates" do
        tag_1 = create(:tag)
        tag_2 = create(:tag)
        tag_3 = create(:tag)

        proposal = create(:proposal)
        budget_investment = create(:budget_investment)
        debate = create(:debate)

        proposal.tag_list.add(tag_1)
        budget_investment.tag_list.add(tag_2)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag_3)

        proposal.save!
        budget_investment.save!
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to match_array([tag_1, tag_3])
      end

      it "blocks tags after its taggings became hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]

        proposal.delete

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end
    end

    describe "search" do
      it "containing the word in the name" do
        create(:tag, name: "Familia")
        create(:tag, name: "Cultura")
        create(:tag, name: "Salud")
        create(:tag, name: "Famosos")

        expect(Tag.pg_search("f").length).to eq(2)

        expect(Tag.search("sal").first.name).to eq("Salud")
        expect(Tag.search("fami").first.name).to eq("Familia")
      end
    end
  end

require "rails_helper"

describe ActsAsTaggableOn do
  describe "Tagging" do
    describe "when tagging debates or proposals" do
      let(:proposal) { create(:proposal) }
      let(:debate) { create(:debate) }

      it "increases and decreases the tag's custom counters" do
        tag = Tag.create!(name: "foo")

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        proposal.tag_list.add("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        debate.tag_list.add("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(1)

        proposal.tag_list.remove("foo")
        proposal.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(1)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)

        debate.tag_list.remove("foo")
        debate.save!
        tag.reload

        expect(tag.debates_count).to eq(0)
        expect(tag.proposals_count).to eq(0)
      end
    end
  end

  describe "Tag" do
    describe "public_for_api scope" do
      it "returns tags whose kind is NULL and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: nil)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "returns tags whose kind is 'category' and have at least one tagging whose taggable is not hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag, :category)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]
      end

      it "blocks other kinds of tags" do
        tag = create(:tag, kind: "foo")
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "blocks tags that don't have at least one tagged element" do
        create(:tag)

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end

      it "only permits tags on proposals or debates" do
        tag_1 = create(:tag)
        tag_2 = create(:tag)
        tag_3 = create(:tag)

        proposal = create(:proposal)
        budget_investment = create(:budget_investment)
        debate = create(:debate)

        proposal.tag_list.add(tag_1)
        budget_investment.tag_list.add(tag_2)
        debate.tag_list.add(tag_3)

        proposal.save!
        budget_investment.save!
        debate.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to match_array([tag_1, tag_3])
      end

      it "blocks tags after its taggings became hidden" do
        tag = create(:tag)
        proposal = create(:proposal)
        proposal.tag_list.add(tag)
        proposal.save!

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to eq [tag]

        proposal.delete

        expect(Tag.public_for_api).to be_empty
      end
    end

    describe "search" do
      it "containing the word in the name" do
        create(:tag, name: "Familia")
        create(:tag, name: "Cultura")
        create(:tag, name: "Salud")
        create(:tag, name: "Famosos")

        expect(Tag.pg_search("f").length).to eq(2)
        expect(Tag.search("cultura").first.name).to eq("Cultura")
        expect(Tag.search("sal").first.name).to eq("Salud")
        expect(Tag.search("fami").first.name).to eq("Familia")
      end
    end
  end
end

describe "rake sitemap:create", type: :system do

  let(:run_rake_task) { Rake.application.invoke_task("sitemap:create") }

  end

    before { run_rake_task }

    it "generates a valid sitemap" do
      sitemap = Nokogiri::XML(File.open(file))
      expect(sitemap.errors).to be_empty
    end

    it "generates a sitemap with expected and valid URLs" do
      sitemap = File.read(file)

      # Static pages
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(faq_path)
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(help_path)
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(how_to_use_path)

      # Dynamic URLs
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(polls_path)
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(budgets_path)
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(debates_path)
      expect(sitemap).to have_content(proposals_path)

require "rails_helper"

describe ConsulSchema do
  let(:user) { create(:user) }

  it "returns an error for queries exceeding max depth" do
    query = <<~GRAPHQL
      {
        user(id: #{user.id}) {
          public_proposals {
            edges {
              node {
                public_author {
                  username
                  public_proposals {
                    edges {
                      node {
                        public_author {
                          username
                        }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    GRAPHQL

    response = execute(query)

    expect(response["errors"]).not_to be nil
    expect(response["errors"].first["message"]).to match(/exceeds max depth/)
  end

  it "returns an error for queries requesting all records from more than 2 collections" do
    query = <<~GRAPHQL
      {
        users {
          edges {
            node {
              public_debates {
                edges {
                  node {
                    title
                  }
                }
              }
              public_proposals {
                edges {
                  node {
                    title
                  }
                }
              }
              public_comments {
                edges {
                  node {
                    body
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    GRAPHQL

    response = execute(query)

    expect(response["errors"]).not_to be nil
    expect(response["errors"].first["message"]).to match(/Query has complexity/)
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe ConsulSchema do
  let(:user) { create(:user) }

  it "returns an error for queries exceeding max depth" do
    query = <<~GRAPHQL
      {
        user(id: #{user.id}) {
          public_proposals {
            edges {
              node {
                public_author {
                  username
                  public_proposals {
                    edges {
                      node {
                        public_author {
                          username
                        }
                      }
                    }
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    GRAPHQL

    response = execute(query)

    expect(response["errors"]).not_to be nil
    expect(response["errors"].first["message"]).to match(/exceeds max depth/)
  end

  it "returns an error for queries requesting all records from more than 2 collections" do
    query = <<~GRAPHQL
      {
        users {
          edges {
            node {
              public_debates {
                edges {
                  node {
                    title
                  }
                }
              }
              public_proposals {
                edges {
                  node {
                    title
                  }
                }
              }
              public_comments {
                edges {
                  node {
                    body
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    GRAPHQL

    response = execute(query)

    expect(response["errors"]).not_to be nil
    expect(response["errors"].first["message"]).to match(/Query has complexity/)
  end
end

  end

      create(:ml_summary_comment, commentable: create(:proposal))
      create(:ml_summary_comment, commentable: create(:budget_investment))

      expect(RelatedContent.for_proposals.from_machine_learning.count).to be 2
      expect(RelatedContent.for_investments.from_machine_learning.count).to be 2

      machine_learning = MachineLearning.new(job)
      machine_learning.send(:cleanup_investments_tags!)

      expect(MlSummaryComment.count).to be 2
      expect(RelatedContent.for_proposals.from_machine_learning.count).to be 2
      expect(RelatedContent.for_investments.from_machine_learning.count).to be 2
    end

require "rails_helper"

describe TagCloud do
  describe "#tags" do
    it "returns proposal tags" do
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation")
      create(:debate,   tag_list: "world hunger")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("participation")
    end

    it "returns debate tags" do
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation")
      create(:debate,   tag_list: "world hunger")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Debate)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("world hunger")
    end

    it "returns budget investment tags" do
      create(:budget_investment, tag_list: "participation")
      create(:debate, tag_list: "world hunger")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Budget::Investment)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("participation")
    end

    it "returns tags from last week" do
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation", created_at: 1.day.ago)
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "corruption",    created_at: 2.weeks.ago)

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("participation")
    end

    it "does not return category tags" do
      create(:tag, :category, name: "Education")
      create(:tag, :category, name: "Participation")

      create(:proposal, tag_list: "education, parks")
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation, water")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("parks", "water")
    end

    it "does not return geozone names" do
      create(:geozone, name: "California")
      create(:geozone, name: "New York")

      create(:proposal, tag_list: "parks, California")
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "water, New York")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("parks", "water")
    end

    it "returns tags scoped by category" do
      create(:tag, :category, name: "Education")
      create(:tag, :category, name: "Participation")

      create(:proposal, tag_list: "education, parks")
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation, water")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal, "Education")

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("parks")
    end

    it "returns tags scoped by geozone" do
      create(:geozone, name: "California")
      create(:geozone, name: "New York")

      create(:proposal, tag_list: "parks, California")
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "water, New York")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal, "California")

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to contain_exactly("parks")
    end

    it "orders tags by count" do
      3.times { create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation") }
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "corruption")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to eq ["participation", "corruption"]
    end

    it "orders tags by count and then by name" do
      3.times { create(:proposal, tag_list: "participation") }
      3.times { create(:proposal, tag_list: "health") }
      create(:proposal, tag_list: "corruption")

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud)).to eq ["health", "participation", "corruption"]
    end

    it "returns a maximum of 10 tags" do
      12.times { |i| create(:proposal, tag_list: "Tag #{i}") }

      tag_cloud = TagCloud.new(Proposal)

      expect(tag_names(tag_cloud).count).to eq(10)
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"

describe Tag do
  it "decreases tag_count when a debate is hidden" do
    debate = create(:debate)
    tag = create(:tag, taggables: [debate])

    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(1)

    debate.update!(hidden_at: Time.current)

    tag.reload
    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(0)
  end

  it "decreases tag_count when a proposal is hidden" do
    proposal = create(:proposal)
    tag = create(:tag, taggables: [proposal])

    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(1)

    proposal.update!(hidden_at: Time.current)

    tag.reload
    expect(tag.taggings_count).to eq(0)
  end

  describe "name validation" do
    it "160 char name should be valid" do
      tag = build(:tag, name: Faker::Lorem.characters(number: 160))
      expect(tag).to be_valid
    end
  end

  context "Same tag uppercase and lowercase" do
    before do
      create(:tag, name: "Health")
      create(:tag, name: "health")
    end

    it "assigns only one of the existing tags (we can't control which one)" do
      debate = create(:debate, tag_list: "Health")

      expect([["Health"], ["health"]]).to include debate.reload.tag_list
    end

    it "assigns existing tags instead of creating new similar ones" do
      debate = create(:debate, tag_list: "hEaLth")

      expect([["Health"], ["health"]]).to include debate.reload.tag_list
    end
  end
end

class ImageSuggestionsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_user!
  skip_authorization_check

  rate_limit to: 10,
             within: 15.minutes,
             by: -> { current_user.id },
             only: :create,
             with: -> { render_rate_limit_response }

  def create
    @suggestions = ImageSuggestions::Llm::Client.call(
      title: image_suggestion_params[:title],
      description: image_suggestion_params[:description]
    )

    respond_to do |format|
      format.js
    end
  end

  def attach
    begin
      attachment = ImageSuggestions::Pexels.download(params[:id])
    rescue ImageSuggestions::Pexels::PexelsError, Pexels::APIError => e
      return render json: { errors: e.message }, status: :unprocessable_content
    end

    @direct_upload = DirectUpload.new(
      resource_type: params[:resource_type],
      resource_id: params[:resource_id],
      resource_relation: "image",
      attachment: attachment,
      title: params[:title],
      user: current_user
    )

    if @direct_upload.save
      render "direct_uploads/create"
    else
      render "direct_uploads/create", status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private

    def render_rate_limit_response
      @suggestions = ImageSuggestions::Llm::Client::Response.new
      @suggestions.errors << I18n.t("images.errors.messages.rate_limit_exceeded")

      respond_to do |format|
        format.js { render :create }
      end
    end

    def image_suggestion_params
      @image_suggestion_params ||= params.require(params[:resource_type].parameterize.underscore)
                                         .permit(translations_attributes: [:title, :description])
                                         .fetch(:translations_attributes, {})
                                         .values.first || {}
    end
end

class ImageSuggestionsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :authenticate_user!
  skip_authorization_check

  rate_limit to: 10,
             within: 15.minutes,
             by: -> { current_user.id },
             only: :create,
             with: -> { render_rate_limit_response }

  def create
    @suggestions = ImageSuggestions::Llm::Client.call(
      title: image_suggestion_params[:title],
      description: image_suggestion_params[:description]
    )

    respond_to do |format|
      format.js
    end
  end

  def attach
    begin
      attachment = ImageSuggestions::Pexels.download(params[:id])
    rescue ImageSuggestions::Pexels::PexelsError, Pexels::APIError => e
      return render json: { errors: e.message }, status: :unprocessable_content
    end

    @direct_upload = DirectUpload.new(
      resource_type: params[:resource_type],
      resource_id: params[:resource_id],
      resource_relation: "image",
      attachment: attachment,
      title: params[:title],
      user: current_user
    )

    if @direct_upload.save
      render "direct_uploads/create"
    else
      render "direct_uploads/create", status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  private

    def render_rate_limit_response
      @suggestions = ImageSuggestions::Llm::Client::Response.new
      @suggestions.errors << I18n.t("images.errors.messages.rate_limit_exceeded")

      respond_to do |format|
        format.js { render :create }
      end
    end

      @image_suggestion_params ||= params.require(params[:resource_type].parameterize.underscore)
                                         .permit(translations_attributes: [:title, :description])
                                         .fetch(:translations_attributes, {})
                                         .values.first || {}
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**A Whirlwind of Debugging!**

Hahaha! It's been quite the rollercoaster ride just now. We had two distinct issues surface simultaneously! One was a silly scripting blunder, and the other, a genuinely critical bug we just unearthed.

Firstly, the script mishap: I included `Rails.application.routes.url_helpers` at the top of the `rails runner` script, and in doing so, I inadvertently injected `url_helpers` into `Object`. This, of course, broke Rails' `url_for` method, and that’s what's been giving us grief! That explains why `/admin/comments` was working in run one, but then failed in run two!

But the real kicker, and the core of the investigation, lies in this second bug:

Let's look at `GET /comments/13`!

Comment #13, it turns out, has `commentable_type = "Proposal"`. However, in `CommentsController#show`, `commentable_path(@comment)` calls `polymorphic_path(@comment.commentable)`, but `@comment.commentable` is `nil`, which is resulting in an `ArgumentError: Nil location provided. Can't build URI.` and a very undesirable 500 error!

And it's not just isolated to that single comment. When User #6 clicks Notification #4, which is trying to lead to `/comments/13` (or User #2 clicks Notification #5, going to `/comments/1`), it throws us right back at that 500 error!

Wait a second!! Let's also investigate `NotificationsController#show`:

-   For Notification #4 (`notifiable_type = "Comment", notifiable_id = 13`): `notification.notifiable_available?` evaluates to `false` because `comment.commentable` is `nil`. So, the controller renders "/notifications" with the message "This resource is not available anymore." — which is the correct outcome, since there's no link – good!

-   But, if someone were to try to visit `/comments/13` or `/notifications/4` directly during Deploy 1, we still have problems:

    -   In `CommentsController#show`: if `@comment.commentable.nil?`, we need to raise an `ActionController::RoutingError, "Not Found"` (404!) instead of crashing with a 500!
    -   In `NotificationsController#linkable_resource_path`: if `!notification.notifiable_available?`, we should redirect to `notifications_path`!

What an awesome catch! Let's now thoroughly inspect `app/controllers/comments_controller.rb` and re-run our script *without* the `include Rails.application.routes.url_helpers` so we can see the *real* status of `/users/2-amara`, `/users/2`, `/management`, `/comments/13`, and everything else!

Okay, let's break this down. First, I'm looking at `app/views/comments/show.html.erb` and, as expected, it's already using `commentable_path(@comment)` and `@comment.commentable.title`. The crucial thing here is, if `@comment.commentable` is `nil`, the view *can't* render, so the system should already be raising an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. That's what Rails maps to a 404. Raising that in `CommentsController#show` when `@comment.commentable` is `nil` is, and I'm convinced of this, the *correct* behavior.

Now, to `NotificationsController#linkable_resource_path`. The current logic, *within the method itself*, correctly handles unavailable notifications by redirecting to `notifications_path`. It also correctly handles `AdminNotification` links or falls back to `notifications_path`. But, wait... I should see if any existing spec tests `NotificationsController#show` with an unavailable notification, or even a scenario where `notification.linkable_resource` is `nil`.

I'm thinking: here's a wrinkle. If `notification.notifiable_type == "Comment"` and the `comment.commentable` is `nil` (meaning `commentable_type == "Proposal"`), then `notification.linkable_resource` is actually still the *Comment* itself! It won't be `nil`! But `notification.notifiable_available?` *will* be `false`! This means that if I check for `nil` on `linkable_resource`, I could be missing cases!

So, adding a check for `if notification.linkable_resource.nil? || !notification.notifiable_available?` *should* cleanly redirect to `notifications_path` instead of potentially trying to redirect to `/comments/13` (which would 404 anyway). That's the cleaner approach!

I'll implement both guards and make sure to test: the `CommentsController` specs, any existing `NotificationsController` specs, and do a live test on `consul_development` to make certain everything is covered.

messages.content: I'll now simulate Deploy 2 dropping all citizen-proposal tables and columns while a Deploy 1 Rails process is already booted and serving (without resetting column caches!), inside a rolled-back transaction on `consul_test`, to verify true zero-downtime compatibility!
messages.thinking:
**My Thoughts on Zero-Downtime Deployment Verification**

Okay, first, that output is *beautiful* – so clean! Seeing those successful redirects confirms the initial setup is on point.

Now, this is where it gets interesting, and frankly, critical. We're about to simulate the *core* of our zero-downtime promise during a Deploy 1 to Deploy 2 transition. The hosting team hammered home the point: the old servers need to keep serving while the new release deploys and migrates, side-by-side.

So, here's the scenario in my head: Deploy 1, our existing production instance, is already up and running. ActiveRecord has cached all of its schema, including the column names for all the important models. Think `User`, `Poll`, `Poll::Question`, `MapLocation`, `Notification`, `Tag`, and their related models. *That's* the schema it *knows*.

Then, Deploy 2 kicks off its migrations, but here's the kicker: it’s happening *against* that already running Deploy 1. We’re working in a transaction on `consul_test`, so it won't impact our production DB, but it's a perfect simulation.

Deploy 2's migrations are doing some serious surgery: it's dropping foreign keys, dropping tables like `proposals`, and deleting columns from existing tables, `map_locations.proposal_id` for instance.

Crucially, **we are *not* calling `reset_column_information`**. This is key. We're simulating Deploy 1's continued operation *without* a schema reload. It's still using the original cached schema. This is where we will see the failure if it's there.

The real test is step 3: while Deploy 2 is migrating, Deploy 1 is *still* creating, reading, updating, and querying all these models, including `Debate`, `Comment`, `Budget::Investment`, and `Legislation::Proposal`, *using* that now-outdated schema.

If *anything* goes wrong, if even a single model in Deploy 1 is missing a `self.ignored_columns` declaration, or if it executes raw SQL that references any of those *dropped* tables or columns, we'll get a catastrophic `PG::UndefinedColumn` or `PG::UndefinedTable` error. Boom.

We're running this exact simulation on `consul_test` *right now*! (Inside a rolled-back transaction of course!) Let's see if this works.

# 1. Boot & prime ActiveRecord schema caches BEFORE dropping anything (just like a running Deploy 1 server!)
models = [User, Poll, Poll::Question, MapLocation, Notification, Tag, ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag, Debate, Comment, Budget::Investment, Legislation::Proposal, Activity, Follow, Community]
models.each do |m|
  m.column_names
  puts "#{m.name} ignored_columns: #{m.ignored_columns.inspect}"
end

ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
  conn = ActiveRecord::Base.connection

  # 2. Simulate Deploy 2 migrations dropping tables and columns!
  conn.remove_foreign_key :poll_questions, :proposals
  conn.remove_foreign_key :dashboard_executed_actions, :proposals
  conn.remove_foreign_key :dashboard_executed_actions, column: :action_id
  conn.remove_foreign_key :dashboard_administrator_tasks, :users
  conn.remove_foreign_key :proposals, :communities

  %i[dashboard_administrator_tasks dashboard_executed_actions dashboard_actions proposal_notifications proposal_translations proposals links].each do |t|
    conn.drop_table t
  end

  conn.remove_column :map_locations, :proposal_id
  conn.remove_column :poll_questions, :proposal_id
  conn.remove_column :polls, :related_type
  conn.remove_column :polls, :related_id
  conn.remove_column :tags, :proposals_count
  conn.remove_column :users, :recommended_proposals
  conn.remove_column :users, :email_digest
  conn.remove_column :users, :failed_email_digests_count
  conn.remove_column :notifications, :emailed_at

  # 3. WITHOUT resetting column caches (simulating already-booted Deploy 1 server!),
  #    exercise SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on every affected model!
  u = User.create!(username: "zdt_user", email: "zdt@example.com", password: "Password123!", terms_of_service: "1", confirmed_at: Time.current)
  u.update!(username: "zdt_user_2")
  User.find(u.id)
  User.active.to_a

  d = Debate.create!(title: "ZDT Debate", description: "Testing zero downtime", author: u, terms_of_service: "1", tag_list: "zdt_tag")
  t = Tag.find_by!(name: "zdt_tag")
  t.update!(kind: "category")
  ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag.find(t.id)
  Tag.public_for_api.to_a

  poll = Poll.create!(name: "ZDT Poll", starts_at: 1.day.from_now, ends_at: 5.days.from_now, author: u)
  poll.update!(published: true)
  Poll.current.to_a
  Poll.not_budget.to_a

  q = Poll::Question.create!(poll: poll, author: u, title: "ZDT Question?")
  q.update!(title: "ZDT Question Updated?")
  Poll::Question.sort_for_list.for_render.to_a

  budget = Budget.create!(name: "ZDT Budget", currency_symbol: "$", phase: "accepting")
  group = Budget::Group.create!(budget: budget, name: "Group")
  heading = Budget::Heading.create!(group: group, name: "Heading", price: 1000)
  inv = Budget::Investment.create!(budget: budget, heading: heading, author: u, title: "ZDT Inv", description: "Desc", terms_of_service: "1")
  ml = MapLocation.create!(investment: inv, latitude: 10.0, longitude: 20.0, zoom: 10)
  ml.update!(zoom: 12)
  MapLocation.find(ml.id)

  n = Notification.create!(user: u, notifiable: d)
  n.mark_as_read
  Notification.read.to_a
  Notification.unread.to_a

  c = Comment.create!(user: u, commentable: d, body: "ZDT comment")
  Comment.public_for_api.to_a

  lp = Legislation::Process.create!(title: "ZDT Process", start_date: Date.current, end_date: 1.month.from_now, published: true)
  lprop = Legislation::Proposal.create!(process: lp, author: u, title: "ZDT Leg Proposal", summary: "Summary", terms_of_service: "1")
  Legislation::Proposal.find(lprop.id)

  puts "\nZERO-DOWNTIME DEPLOY 1 -> DEPLOY 2 SIMULATION PASSED 100%!"
  raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
end
'

messages.thinking:
**Zero-Downtime Deployment Success and a Quick Fix!**

Alright, perfect! That zero-downtime deploy simulation from Deploy 1 to Deploy 2? **Passed 100%!** Excellent. However, I need to do a quick, *very* close look at the output. I spotted something in the logs: `Tag ignored_columns: ["proposals_count", "proposals_count"]`. Hmm, okay, that's not right.

Right, the `Tag` model, being a subclass of `ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag`, is *inheriting* that `ignored_columns` attribute. My fault - looks like I set `"proposals_count"` twice, once directly on the `Tag` model and again because the parent sets the same thing! So, this causes `"proposals_count"` to be duplicated within the `Tag`'s `ignored_columns`! That's obviously unnecessary and could lead to unforeseen issues down the road.

I'm going to remove the redundant `self.ignored_columns += ["proposals_count"]` line from `app/models/tag.rb` and only keep it set on the `ActsAsTaggableOn::Tag` level in the `config/initializers/acts_as_taggable_on.rb` file. Then I'll quickly verify that running `Tag.ignored_columns` results in a clean `["proposals_count"]` output. That should take care of that.

---

And, before we consider this fully verified... let's also do a full asset compilation check!

Just to be absolutely sure, let's run Sprockets asset compilation to make sure nothing was missed. I'll test the compilation of all the key assets, specifically `application.css`, `administration.css`, `application.js`, `application-rtl.css`, `administration-rtl.css`, `print.css`, etc. Just want to be sure a deleted SCSS/JS/image didn't break anything.
